fields.name: Bran Castle
fields.description: Perched on a rocky hilltop in the Carpathian Mountains, Bran Castle is Romania's most visited landmark and is commonly associated with the legend of Dracula. Built in the 14th century, it served as a royal residence for Queen Marie of Romania.

fields.name: Black Sea Beach
fields.description: Located on the western shore of the Black Sea, Constanta is Romania's oldest continuously inhabited city and its largest port. The beach resort area attracts millions of visitors each summer with its warm waters, sandy shores and vibrant nightlife along the Romanian Riviera.

fields.name: National Museum of Art Bucharest
fields.description: Houses an extensive collection of Romanian and European art, located in the former Royal Palace on Calea Victoriei.

fields.name: Peles Castle
fields.description: A stunning Neo-Renaissance castle in the Carpathian Mountains, built as a summer residence for King Carol I in the 19th century.

fields.name: Sighisoara Citadel
fields.description: A medieval fortified city and UNESCO World Heritage Site, birthplace of Vlad the Impaler, featuring colourful buildings and a clock tower.

fields.name: Danube Delta
fields.description: One of Europe's largest and best-preserved deltas, a UNESCO biosphere reserve home to thousands of bird species and diverse wildlife.

fields.name: Central Park
fields.description: A large urban park in the heart of Cluj-Napoca featuring a lake, casino building and recreational areas popular with locals and tourists.

fields.name: St. Michael's Church
fields.description: A Gothic Roman Catholic church dating from the 14th century, one of the most important Gothic monuments in Transylvania.

fields.name: Merry Cemetery
fields.description: A unique cemetery in Sapanta featuring colourful wooden crosses with naive paintings and humorous epitaphs describing the deceased's life.

fields.name: Wooden Churches
fields.description: A unique cemetery in Sapanta featuring colourful wooden crosses with naive paintings and humorous epitaphs describing the deceased's life.

fields.name: Black Church
fields.description: The largest Gothic church in Romania, named after fire damage from 1689, containing a famous collection of Anatolian carpet

fields.name: Tampa Mountain
fields.description: A mountain overlooking Brasov city with a cable car and hiking trails, offering panoramic views of the historic old town below.

fields.name: Viscri White Church
fields.description: A 12th century fortified Saxon church and UNESCO World Heritage Site, one of Romania's best preserved medieval structures surrounded by traditional village life.

fields.name: Place Of Culture
fields.description: A stunning neo-Gothic palace in the heart of lasi, completed in 1925. It houses four museums and is one of Romania’s most iconic landmarks.

fields.name: Place Of Parliament
fields.description: The Palace of the Parliament is the world's second largest administrative building, built under Nicolae Ceaușescu in the 1980s. It contains over 1,000 rooms and is a symbol of Romania's communist era.
